channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [7] Spin order steers a light–matter condensate
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Hui Deng

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magnetic control of condensates in the layered vdW magnet CrSBr; relevant material class.

Tags: #CrSBr #magnetism #vdWmaterials

Abstract: Light–matter condensates get a magnetic control knob. In the layered magnet CrSBr, reorienting the spins with a modest field shifts the condensate’s colour by more than 10 meV.

item.title: [6] Nonlinear waveguide polaritons for long-distance propagation of spins at room temperature
item.content:encoded:
Authors: Authors not available in source RSS

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Spin propagation in TMD-based waveguides, relevant to the user's 2D material interests.

Tags: #TMD #spintronics #polaritons

Abstract: In spintronics, the spin of particles is used to transfer information but the propagation distances are short, whereas photons carry spin further but lack the nonlinear interactions necessary for logic gates. Now, polariton waveguides built from transition metal dichalcogenides enable spin propagation of up to 100 μm at room temperature and maintain large polariton nonlinearities.

item.title: [6] Spin currents in polariton waveguides driven by bright and dark excitons
item.description:
Last authors: Weibo Gao, Jesús Zúñiga-Pérez

Authors: Qiuyu Shang, Mingyang Zhang, Maria V. Maggi, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Observations of the optical spin Hall effect in monolayer WS2 polaritonic waveguides.

Tags: #TMDC #topology #spintronics

Abstract: The optical spin Hall effect enables the spatial separation of four domains of circularly polarized light from a linearly polarized source through photonic spinâorbit coupling, which arises from non-degenerate transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic modes. This mechanism is ineffective for incoherent photoluminescence. In transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers, bright excitons possess in-plane electric dipoles and strong oscillator strengths, whereas dark excitons have out-of-plane dipoles. Here, by embedding WS2 monolayers in waveguide microcavities, we demonstrate strong coupling between bright excitons and photonic modes, forming excitonâpolaritons. Under non-resonant pumping, dark excitons become strongly populated and feed both transverse-magnetic- and transverse-electric-like excitonâpolariton modes, each with an out-of-plane electric-field component. We observe the optical spin Hall effect in waveguide polaritons, leading to the formation of eight polarization domains and spin-polarized polariton currents propagating up to 92âÂ±â1âÎ¼m at room temperature. These results establish transition metal dichalcogenide-based polaritonic waveguides as a promising platform for room-temperature spin-optoelectronic devices.

item.title: [8] Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
item.description:
Last authors: Hong-Jun Gao, Wu Zhou

Authors: Meng Gao, Deping Guo, Ang Li, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Reports synthesis of monolayer metal oxides with predicted antiferromagnetism and excitonic responses.

Tags: #2D-materials #magnetism #heterostructures

Abstract: Two-dimensional metal oxides offer a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena and enable functionalities beyond those of their bulk counterparts. Despite advances in synthesizing ultrathin and free-standing oxides, controlled fabrication at the single-atomic-layer limit has remained a formidable challenge. Here we report the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides (MO), including CrO, ErO and BiO, down to the single-atomic-layer limit via electron-beam-induced dehalogenation of layered metal oxyhalides (MOX). Using monolayer CrO as a representative system, which features a single-atomic-layer square lattice, we obtain free-standing single-crystalline domains exceeding 104ânm2 and demonstrate controllable patterning at the micrometre scale. Density functional theory confirms both the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of free-standing monolayer CrO, predicting a NÃ©el antiferromagnetic order below 230âK. Combined experimental and theoretical analysis reveals that ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation underpin the CrOCl-to-CrO transformation, a conversion mechanism potentially extendable to other metal oxyhalides. This approach further enables the fabrication of MOXâMO lateral heterostructures as well as aligned and twisted metal oxide bilayers, which exhibit pronounced excitonic responses with an unusually large exciton binding energy. Our work opens opportunities for two-dimensional metal oxide monolayers, heterostructures and moirÃ© superlattices, and for exploring emergent excitonic phenomena in low-dimensional oxides.

item.title: [9] Altermagnetic signatures and topological textures in ultrathin multiferroic BiFeO3
item.description:
Last authors: Angela Wittmann, Lucas Caretta

Authors: Geo Fratian, Maya Ramesh, Xinyan Li, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Directly features altermagnetism and spin-resolved photoemission, both core interests in the user's profile.

Tags: #spin-resolvedphotoemission #BiFeO3 #altermagnetism

Abstract: Magnetoelectric multiferroics promise low-power switching, non-volatile memory and signal transduction, yet practical deployment requires ultrathin films in which polar and magnetic order often degrade. Uncompensated bound charge drives depolarization in ferroelectrics, whereas off-stoichiometry, reduced anisotropy and charge transfer can produce magnetic dead layers. Here we realize a multiferroic phase of BiFeO3 with no dead layer, revealing signatures of emergent altermagnetism in the ultrathin limit. First-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomic-resolution imaging and magnetic imaging show that short-circuit electrostatic boundary conditions and epitaxial strain drive a continuous, thickness-induced phase transition accompanied by multiferroic topological textures. At four unit cells, these boundary conditions stabilize a collinear monoclinic phase with d-wave altermagnetic order, supported by magnetic circular dichroism and spin-resolved photoemission measurements. These results establish a pathway to stabilize unconventional multiferroicity at device-relevant thicknesses, reframing scaling limits for oxide electronics.

item.title: [7] Magnetic control of an exciton–polariton condensate in a van der Waals magnet
item.description:
Last authors: Florian Dirnberger, Rupert Huber

Authors: Heng Zhang, Niloufar Nilforoushan, Christian Weidgans, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important study on a van der Waals magnet (CrSBr) relevant to the user's 2D materials interest.

Tags: #material #CrSBr #exciton-polaritons

Abstract: Quasiparticle condensates are among the most striking solid-state manifestations of quantum physics. Coupling macroscopic real-space wavefunctions to additional degrees of freedom, such as the electron spin, would add valuable control knobs for quantum applications. While creating spin-carrying superconducting condensates has attracted enormous attention, condensates of light-matter hybrids known as exciton–polaritons have lacked an analogous spin-based perspective. Here we demonstrate magnetically tunable exciton–polariton condensation in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr. Under photoexcitation, CrSBr microwires embedded in an optical cavity show the hallmarks of polariton condensation. Owing to the strong coupling between the spin order and excitonic correlation, the energy of the condensate can be tuned by up to 10.5 meV by an external magnetic field of 2 T. Our results establish CrSBr microcavities as a powerful platform for exploring magnetic control of polariton condensates and mark an essential step towards spin-controlled coherent quantum light sources.

item.title: [9] Ultrafast anisotropic valleytronics in SnSe
item.description:
Last authors: Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu

Authors: Yiming Pan, Sotirios Fragkos, Dominique Descamps, Stéphane Petit, Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Uses time-resolved ARPES to study electronic dynamics in an anisotropic quantum material.

Tags: #method #tr-ARPES #SnSe

Abstract: Understanding and controlling valley-specific lightâmatter interactions and non-equilibrium microscopic coupling mechanisms lie at the heart of valleytronics. Due to their strong in-plane anisotropy, which enables polarization-controlled optical transitions to distinct non-degenerate valleys, group-IV monochalcogenides have been recently proposed as promising candidates for next-generation valleytronic materials. However, ultrafast non-equilibrium dynamics following the optical preparation of valley-polarized states have received limited attention in these systems. Here, combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with time-dependent Boltzmann equation simulations, we investigate ultrafast valley polarization dynamics following polarization-controlled photoexcitation in SnSe. We show that selective excitation to valleys at global conduction minima yields nearly unity and time-independent valley polarization. By contrast, photoexcitation to the other valley channel leads to ultrafast decay and reversal of valley polarization on subpicosecond timescales due to intervalley scattering mediated by strong electronâphonon coupling with an optical phonon mode. Our findings reveal strongly anisotropic and radically different non-equilibrium valley physics than in most common two-dimensional valleytronics materials.
